title: Locate the Cavite Event
imageAlt: Modern labelled case diagram: Locate the Cavite Event. No violence or original document is depicted.
content:
Our new case starts at Cavite on 20 January 1872. A mutiny is a military uprising against authority. The NHCP execution-site marker links the later accusation against three priests with this January event.

Keep two places separate: Cavite is linked with the uprising; Bagumbayan in Manila is linked with the later execution. Related events in the same year are not necessarily the same event. This introductory timeline does not settle every disagreement about the causes or extent of the uprising.

Your museum task is to locate the event accurately. We study what happened without acting as fighters.
clues: Place: Cavite, separate from the later Manila event.
task: Which label starts this case timeline?
20 January 1872: military uprising in Cavite.
17 February 1872: publication of a newspaper.
20 January 1872: dedication of a novel.
17 February 1872: opening of the Suez Canal.
reason: The Cavite Mutiny was a military uprising on 20 January 1872; the later execution was a separate event.

title: Meet the Three Priests
definition: A combined name remembering Mariano Gomes, Jose Burgos and Jacinto Zamora.
imageAlt: Modern labelled case diagram: Meet the Three Priests. No violence or original document is depicted.
content:
GOMBURZA combines parts of three surnames: Gomes, Burgos and Zamora. Mariano Gomes, Jose Burgos and Jacinto Zamora were three Filipino priests. Some historical writing uses Gomez for Gomes; in this lesson these spellings refer to the same priest.

The NHCP connects their memory with secularization and equal rights. Recall the previous mission: secularization concerns parish administration by secular clergy. Supporting reform does not by itself establish that someone organized a military uprising.

Keep the people card separate from the event card. The combined name remembers three people, not every participant in the Cavite Mutiny.
clues: People: the three priests Gomes, Burgos and Zamora.
Limit: supporting reform does not prove mutiny leadership.
task: Which people belong on the GOMBURZA card?
Mariano Gomes, Jose Burgos and Jacinto Zamora.
Pedro Pelaez, Jose Rizal and Marcelo del Pilar.
Isabelo de los Reyes, Jose Rizal and Andres Bonifacio.
The crew of every ship arriving at Cavite.
reason: GOMBURZA remembers the three priests; reform advocacy alone does not prove involvement in the mutiny.

title: Read the Accusation Carefully
definition: A claim of wrongdoing that must be examined using evidence.
imageAlt: Modern labelled case diagram: Read the Accusation Carefully. No violence or original document is depicted.
content:
After the uprising, colonial authorities accused the priests of involvement. The NHCP marker describes their involvement as alleged. Alleged means claimed, rather than proven merely by saying it. The National Museum describes suspected treason: a charge of acting against the government to which a person owes allegiance.

A caption should distinguish the accusation from proof. A serious punishment does not by itself prove that an accusation was true. Our classroom cards cannot replace examination of historical records.

Repair this fictional label: "They were accused, so they must have organized the mutiny." An accusation and a proven action are different. You are not asked to decide guilt from three short clues.
clues: Claim: authorities linked the priests with the uprising.
Language: alleged involvement means claimed involvement.
Reasoning: punishment alone cannot prove the accused action.
task: Which caption handles the accusation carefully?
Authorities accused the priests; the accusation itself is not proof they organized the mutiny.
An accusation automatically proves every detail of a case.
A later monument proves that no uprising took place.
Anyone supporting reform must have led the mutiny.
reason: Distinguish the authorities' accusation from evidence of an action; accusation or punishment alone does not prove involvement.

title: Place the Loss on the Timeline
definition: The order in which events happened.
imageAlt: Modern labelled case diagram: Place the Loss on the Timeline. No violence or original document is depicted.
content:
The three priests were executed at Bagumbayan in Manila on 17 February 1872. Executed means put to death under a government sentence. This was a serious loss of human life. We remember it respectfully, without showing or acting out how it happened.

The January uprising came first; the February execution followed. Both belong to 1872, but they happened on different days and in different places. Modern memorials remember this loss.

The timeline helps explain the sequence. It is not a countdown or a battle. Your task is to explain what happened first and what followed, while keeping a claim of involvement separate from proof.
clues: Later: 17 February 1872, execution at Bagumbayan, Manila.
Respect: explaining a loss does not make harm a game goal.
task: Which timeline keeps the events in order?
Cavite Mutiny in January, then execution at Bagumbayan in February 1872.
Execution in January, then the Cavite Mutiny in February 1872.
Both events happened at the same place on the same day.
The execution happened before Spanish colonial rule began.
reason: The 20 January mutiny preceded the 17 February execution at Bagumbayan in 1872.

title: Build a Remembrance Case Board
definition: An act that keeps the memory of people or events alive.
imageAlt: Modern labelled case diagram: Build a Remembrance Case Board. No violence or original document is depicted.
content:
Jose Rizal dedicated his second novel, El Filibusterismo, to the memory of the priests. In the dedication he questioned the accusation. This gives evidence of his response, not every Filipino's opinion.

The NHCP also records remembrance within the Katipunan. These responses connect the case with wider concerns for justice and the country. They do not mean one event alone caused every later movement, or that everyone responded alike.

Build a modern case board. Connect an event, a claim and a later response with the kind of information each provides. Then explain why a dedication is evidence of remembrance, not proof that its writer witnessed the uprising.
clues: Later writing: Rizal dedicated El Filibusterismo to the priests.
Wider concern: remembrance connected the case with justice and the country.
Limit: a dedication does not show everyone held the same view.
task: What does Rizal's dedication help us understand?
He honored the priests and questioned the accusation in his later writing.
He personally witnessed every part of the Cavite Mutiny.
Every Filipino had an identical opinion of the case.
The dedication itself proves the priests organized the mutiny.
reason: Rizal's dedication records remembrance and concern about injustice; it does not prove eyewitness knowledge or a single nationwide response.

title: Explain the Whole Case
definition: An account connecting events and responses while showing what evidence supports.
imageAlt: Modern labelled case diagram: Explain the Whole Case. No violence or original document is depicted.
content:
Your case has three parts. Locate the Cavite Mutiny on 20 January 1872. Explain that authorities accused Gomes, Burgos and Zamora, and that the priests were executed at Bagumbayan on 17 February. Then identify later remembrance, such as Rizal's dedication.

The sequence connects events without confusing them. Punishment does not turn an accusation into proof. Later remembrance helps explain why the case remained important in concerns about justice and the country.

Complete this report frame silently or with a trusted adult: "The event was ___. The accusation was ___. A later response was ___. It shows ___, but does not prove ___." The quiz checks five lesson topics. If one is difficult, review its scene before targeted practice.
clues: Distinguish: an event and the people accused are different subjects.
Sequence: January mutiny, February execution, later remembrance.
Explain: connect a response with justice and state its limits.
task: Which report connects the case evidence?
A January mutiny was followed by accusations and a February execution; later remembrance expressed concern about injustice.
A novel dedication was the mutiny and happened before January 1872.
All reform supporters certainly organized the uprising.
One memorial tells us every detail of the trial and every person's view.
reason: A sound explanation distinguishes the event, accusation, execution and later remembrance.
